numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Timestamp.min.value scale: seconds near -9223372036855 multiplied by 10**6 overflows int64 in scaleSecondsToMicroseconds; the reproducer ts Timestamp('-290308-12-21 19:59:05.224193') built from pd.Timestamp.min.value with unit='us'
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: ts = pd.Timestamp(pd.Timestamp.min.value, unit="us"); per = pd.Period(ts, freq="us") raises OverflowError at np_datetime.c:458 instead of constructing a Period
Reported incorrect result: per displays Period('1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000', 'us') rather than the min timestamp's own fields, showing a wrong value after the intermediate int64 overflow

Reporter's analysis: seconds = -9223372036855 is multiplied by 10**6 in scaleSecondsToMicroseconds and overflows, with the subsequent addition of dts->us expected to reverse the overflow, which is not valid two's-complement reasoning for this path

Fix splits the computation: min_scalable_seconds = NPY_MIN_INT64 / 1000000, seconds_below_threshold = seconds - min_scalable_seconds, scaled_us = us_per_second * (seconds - seconds_below_threshold), then checked_add of the parts, relying on identity y = a*(x+k) + (b - a*k) with k > 0

Regression test test_construction_from_min_timestamp asserts per.year, month, day, hour, minute, second equal those of ts; to_timestamp round-trip is commented out due to OutOfBoundsDatetime (-290308-12-21 19:59:05 out of nanosecond range)
Overflow checks PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW are the relevant guards; reviewer asked whether a test can hit either overflow check
reproduction_risks: The fixed-point 1970-01-01 result in the bug report is the wrong value to check against; the expected fields come from ts, not from the buggy output
Round-trip via to_timestamp is out of nanosecond bounds and cannot be used as an oracle
Passages give no explicit expected numeric output for the corrected Period beyond the field values of ts
Exact sign and magnitude of the int64 intermediate is only approximate in the reporter's comment

provenance.value: Creating a Period from a near-minimum microsecond Timestamp raises OverflowError (Overflow occurred at ../../pandas/_libs/src/vendored/numpy/datetime/np_datetime.c:458) instead of returning a Period; the overflow occurs in the seconds-to-microseconds conversion (scaleSecondsToMicroseconds multiplying seconds=-9223372036855 by 10**6) in npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime, and in the reproducer the period displayed is Period('1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000', 'us'), which is wrong.

The conversion should handle the recoverable overflow for near-minimum timestamps with microsecond resolution and produce the correct Period rather than raising or yielding 1970-01-01; the fix adds a split of the scaled value into two parts so that no intermediate overflow occurs.
